title: acmella buphthalmoides
intro: Acmella buphthalmoides, commonly known as 'parlor weed' or 'spoonleaf', is a plant species in the daisy family (Asteraceae) native to the tropical regions of Central and South America. It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, including treating various health issues such as fever, rheumatism, and digestive problems. The plant's health benefits include its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antispasmodic properties, which are attributed to its therapeutic actions of soothing pain, reducing inflammation, and relaxing muscles. The bioactive constituents of Acmella buphthalmoides include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal and therapeutic effects.
